question: What is the primary physical function of the integumentary system?

options.A: Synthesizing all essential human vitamins independently
options.B: Pumping oxygenated blood throughout deep tissue layers
options.C: Providing a protective barrier against external hazards
options.D: Producing white blood cells for the immune response

explanation: The integumentary system primarily acts as a shield protecting internal body structures from pathogens, chemicals, and physical injury. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is skin assessment particularly valuable during a general nursing physical examination?

options.A: It provides a definitive measurement of internal core body temperature
options.B: It directly measures the exact rate of cellular metabolism
options.C: It accurately determines the total white blood cell count
options.D: It gives immediate clues about hydration and systemic health

explanation: Changes in skin color, turgor, and moisture reflect underlying fluid balance, circulation, and overall medical conditions. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which epidermal layer contains actively dividing stem cells?
explanation: The stratum basale rests on the basement membrane and houses the mitotic stem cells that continuously supply new cells to upper layers. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h2)

question: Where is the stratum lucidum typically located on the human body?

options.C: Palms and soles of the feet

explanation: This clear layer of dead keratinocytes is exclusively found in areas subjected to heavy friction, such as thick skin on palms and soles. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h2)

question: What type of tissue primarily makes up the reticular layer of the dermis?
explanation: The reticular layer consists of thick bundles of collagen and elastin fibers arranged in a dense irregular network that provides strength in multiple directions. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary function of dermal papillae in the papillary layer?

options.A: Storing excess fat for long-term energy reserves
options.B: Producing melanin pigment to protect against UV rays
options.C: Secreting oily sebum to lubricate skin surfaces
options.D: Forming unique fingerprints and housing touch receptors

explanation: Dermal papillae create interlocking ridges with the epidermis, forming fingerprint patterns and bringing blood vessels and nerve endings close to the surface. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h3)

question: What primary tissue type dominates the hypodermis layer?
explanation: The hypodermis contains a large amount of fat-storing adipose cells that provide insulation, padding, and energy storage. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is the hypodermis chosen as the anatomical site for subcutaneous insulin injections?

options.A: It lacks any nerve fibers, preventing pain during needle insertion
options.B: It has a loose structure with slow, steady absorption rates
options.C: It contains massive blood vessels for instant systemic distribution
options.D: It actively neutralizes injected medications before they work

explanation: The loose connective and fatty nature of the hypodermis allows injected medications to be absorbed gradually into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which gland type is primarily responsible for cooling the body through watery sweat production?
explanation: Eccrine glands are distributed all over the skin surface and secrete a watery fluid that cools the body down when body temperature rises. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary function of sebum produced by sebaceous glands?

options.A: Producing vitamin D precursors using sunlight exposure
options.B: Anchoring hair shafts securely into the dermal layer
options.C: Lubricating and waterproofing the skin and hair
options.D: Regulating core body temperature during heavy fevers

explanation: Sebum is an oily substance that prevents skin and hair from drying out while also providing mild antibacterial properties. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which skin receptors are primarily responsible for detecting deep pressure and vibration?
explanation: Pacinian corpuscles are mechanoreceptors located deep in the dermis that sense deep pressure and high-frequency vibration. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h6)

question: What physiological action does the skin take when core body temperature drops significantly?

options.A: Dermal blood vessels dilate to release excess heat
options.B: Sebaceous glands secrete more oily sebum onto the surface
options.C: Dermal blood vessels constrict to conserve core heat
options.D: Eccrine sweat glands increase production of watery sweat

explanation: Vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin surface, minimizing heat loss from the blood to the external environment. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h6)
